name: gb_nib_past_wall_end — GB anchorage nib may extend past the wall end (field bug 2026-08-11)

bug: Reported from the live site: entering e_L = 3 in on the default geometry returned
'GEOM e_L would extend GB beyond wall end' and blanked the drawing. That rule was wrong.
In the default geometry the bearing outer face sits exactly at the wall end
(x_L = 15 in, lb_L/2 = 15 in -> outer face at x = 0), so the old rule forced e_L = 0 and made
the extension input unusable — while extending the grade beam past the wall end is exactly the
standard nib detail for developing a hooked tie bar (PLAN 5 / ACI 318-19 23.8.3).
New rule: e >= 0, and the NIB (length past the wall end, = e - o where o is the wall's own
extension beyond the bearing outer face) is capped at min(h_gb, lb) — the SAME limit as the
outboard-strip dispersion rule (AUDIT-FIXES E), so the nib's weight reaches the bearing instead
of acting as a designed cantilever. Where the wall itself continues past the bearing (outboard
strip / Case C overhang) the GB merely follows the wall and e is unbounded (Case C uses e = 96).
datum_trap: Caught in pre-deploy verification: strip.len is measured wall-end -> bearing CENTERLINE, while e
is measured from the bearing OUTER face. The nib self-weight term must therefore use
e - strip.o (o = max(0, len - lb/2)), NOT e - strip.len, which understates the nib by lb/2 and
silently contributed ZERO weight for any nib shorter than lb/2 (i.e. every realistic nib).
Run 3 exists specifically so that this term cannot regress unnoticed.
hand: Run 1 (nib_develops_unconfined_hook) — the design the user was chasing: unconfined hook (psi_r = 1.6).
psi_r forced to 1.6 by using 6 tie bars: s_hooked = (24 - 2*2 - 1)/(6-1) = 3.80 in < 6db = 6.0 in,
and ties at 100 in o.c. give Ath = 1 set * 2 legs * 0.11 = 0.22 < 0.4*Ahs, so neither disjunct of
Table 25.4.3.2 is met -> psi_r = 1.6.
ldh = (fy*psi_e*psi_r*psi_o*psi_c/(55*lambda*sqrt(f'c))) * db^1.5
Available with e_L = 3: x_crit + lb + e - cover_side. Tie centroid y_t = 3 + 0.5 = 3.5 in.
With e = 0 the same model gives available 29.4589 in (DCR 1.0817, FAIL) — the reported failure.
So a 3 in nib is precisely what turns the unconfined-hook design from failing to passing.
(29.4589 / 32.4589 / 0.98178 are hand values carrying rounded-theta error; the engine gives
32.46032 / 0.981737. Both sit inside the stated rtol — the asserts are not exact-to-the-digit.)
Run 2 (nib_over_limit_rejected): nib = 24.6 - 0 = 24.6 > min(h_gb, lb) = min(24, 30) = 24
-> GEOM error, nib out of scope.
Run 3 (nib_self_weight_in_bearing) — locks the self-weight term the datum trap above defeated:
e_L = 20, e_R = 0 on the default geometry. o_L = x_L - lb_L/2 = 15 - 15 = 0, so nib_L = 20 in
Bearing envelope governs at 1.2D+1.6L (1.4D gives only 11.515 klf vs 18.198 klf), so f_D = 1.2:
R_bearing,R (e_R = 0, nib 0) stays 259.3215 kip — proves the term is per-side, not global.
Under the OLD buggy formula nib would be max(0, 20 - 15) = 5 -> 0.30 kip -> RbL 259.6215,
so this assert fails loudly if the datum regresses.

values.note: nib = e_L - o_L = 20 - 0 (outer-face datum; e - strip.len would give 5)
e_R = 0 -> no nib on the right
truss reaction unaffected by the nib
